records.signal_description: CF to debt; Sum of income before extraordinary items (ib) and depreciation and amortization (dp) divided by total liabilities (lt) averaged over the current and previous fiscal years.

records.name: Cash-based oper prof lagged assets
records.signal_description: Cash-based oper prof lagged assets; Revenue (revt) minus cost (cogs) - (administrative expenses (xsga) - R&D expenses (xrd))  minus annual change in receivables (rect), annual change in investment (invt) and annual change in prepaid expenses, plus annual change in current deferred revenue (drc), long-term deferred revenue (drlt), accounts payable (ap) and accrued expenses (xacc), all divided by total assets (at) in year t-1. Replace all variables in the numerator with 0 if they are missing. Exclude if share code is greater 11, market value of equity, BM or total assets are missing, or if SIC code between 6000 and 6999.

records.name: Cash-based oper prof lagged assets qtrly
records.signal_description: Cash-based oper prof lagged assets qtrly; Revenue (revtq) minus cost (cogsq) - (administrative expenses (xsgaq) - R&D expenses (xrdq))  minus annual change in receivables (rectq), annual change in investment (invtq) and annual change in prepaid expenses, plus annual change in current deferred revenue (drcq), long-term deferred revenue (drlt), accounts payable (apq) and accrued expenses (xaccq), all divided by total assets (atq) in previous quarter. Replace all variables in the numerator with 0 if they are missing. Exclude if share code is greater 11, market value of equity, BM or total assets are missing, or if SIC code between 6000 and 6999.

records.name: Operating Cash flows to price quarterly
records.signal_description: Operating Cash flows to price quarterly; Operating cash-flow (oancf) divided by market value of equity. If operating cash-flow is missing, replace by difference betwee net income (ib) and level of accruals, where the latter is the annual change in current assets (act) minus the annual change in cash and short-term investments (che), minus the annual change in current liabilities (lct) plus the annual change in debt in current liabilities (dlc) plus the annual change in payable income taxes (txp) plus depreciation (dp).

records.name: Cash flow to market quarterly
records.signal_description: Cash flow to market quarterly; Net income (ib) plus depreciation (dp) divided by market equity. Exclude NASDAQ stocks.

records.name: Change in Return on assets
records.signal_description: Change in Return on assets; Quarterly return on assets (rdq/atq) minus its value four quarters ago.

records.name: Change in Return on equity
records.signal_description: Change in Return on equity; Quarterly return on equity (ceqq/atq) minus its value four quarters ago.

records.name: Change in Noncurrent Operating Assets
records.signal_description: Change in Noncurrent Operating Assets; Twelve-month change in noncurrent operating assets. Noncurrent operating assets is ( (at - act - ivao) - (lt - dlc - dltt) )/at.

records.name: Change in Noncurrent Operating Liab
records.signal_description: Change in Noncurrent Operating Liab; Twelve-month change in noncurrent operating liabilites. Noncurrent operating liabilites is (lt - dlc- dltt).

records.name: Change in Profit Margin
records.signal_description: Change in Profit Margin; Annual change in profit margin PM (profit margin defined below). Exclude if price less than 5.

records.name: Current Ratio
records.signal_description: Current Ratio; Current total assets (act) divided by current total liabilities (lct). If missing, replace current total assets by cash and short-term investments (che) plus total receivables (rect) plus total inventory (invt), and replace current total liabilities (lct) with accounts payable (ap).

records.name: Depreciation to PPE
records.signal_description: Depreciation to PPE; Depreciation and amortization (dp) divided by property, plant and equipment net total (ppent).

records.name: Dividend yield for small stocks
records.signal_description: Dividend yield for small stocks; Define tempDY as 4 times latest dividend (divamt) divided by price (prc). Define positive yield stocks as those which paid a dividend in all of the past 4 quarters.  Set DivYield to missing if stock is above the median firm size.  This procedure is based on Table 1B.

records.name: Last year's dividends over price
records.signal_description: Last year's dividends over price

records.name: Earnings conservatism
records.signal_description: Earnings conservatism; Earnings (ib) scaled by market capitalization (shrout*abs(prc)) regressed on the 15 month stock return from (t=-11 to t=+3), an indicator for whether that 15- month return is negative and the interaction of these two variables. Rolling regression in annual data with 10 observations. EarningsConservatism is the sum of the coefficients on the 15-month stock return and the interaction term divided by the coefficient on the 15-month stock return.

records.name: Earnings persistence
records.signal_description: Earnings persistence; Earnings per share (epspx/ajex) regressed on its value from the previous year. Rolling regression in annual data with 10 observations. EarningsPersistence is the coefficient on the lagged value.

records.name: Earnings Predictability
records.signal_description: Earnings Predictability; Earnings per share (epspx/ajex) regressed on its value from the previous year. Rolling regression in annual data with 10 observations. EarningsPredictability is the R2 of this regression.

records.name: Earnings Smoothness
records.signal_description: Earnings Smoothness; 10-year rolling standard deviation of (ib/at) divided by 10-year rolling standard deviation of cash-flow ((ib - ( (act - act_{t-1}) - (lct - lct_{t-1}) - (che - che_{t-1}) + (dlc - dlc_{t-1}) - dp))/at_{t-1})

records.name: Earnings timeliness
records.signal_description: Earnings timeliness; Earnings (ib) scaled by market capitalization (shrout*abs(prc)) regressed on the 15 month stock return from (t=-11 to t=+3), an indicator for whether that 15- month return is negative and the interaction of these two variables. Rolling regression in annual data with 10 observations. EarningsTimeliness is the R2 of this regression.

records.name: Value relevance of earnings
records.signal_description: Value relevance of earnings; 15 month stock return from (t=-11 to t=+3) regressed on Earnings (ib) and the change in earnings, both scaled by market capitalization (shrout*abs(prc)). Rolling regression in annual data with 10 observations. EarningsValueRelevance is the R2 of this regression.

records.name: Enterprise component of BM
records.signal_description: Enterprise component of BM; (ceq + che - dltt - dlc - dc - dvpa+ tstkp ) / (mve\_c + che - dltt - dlc - dc - dvpa+ tstkp). Exclude if price less than 5.

records.name: Enterprise Multiple quarterly
records.signal_description: Enterprise Multiple quarterly; Market value of equity + long-term debt (dltt) + debt in current liabilities (dlc) + deferred charges (dc) - cash and short-term investments (che) , divided by operating income (oibdp). Exclude if missing book equity or negative operating income.

records.name: Earnings-to-Price Ratio
records.signal_description: Earnings-to-Price Ratio; ib / lag(market value of equity, 6 months).  NYSE stocks only.  Exclude if EP < 0.  Lag simulates the Dec 31 market equity used in original paper

records.name: Effective Tax Rate
records.signal_description: Effective Tax Rate; Let Tax be tax payments (txt) over pre-tax income (pi) and amortization of intangibles (am, 0 if missing). Let earnings per share be epspx/ajex. ETR if Tax minus the average of Tax over the previous three years multiplied by one-year EPS growth scaled by by price (prcc_f).

records.name: Failure probability
records.signal_description: Failure probability; Failure probability is -9.16 -.058*PRICE + .075*MB - 2.13*CASHMTA -.045*RSIZE + 1.41*IdioRisk - 7.13*EXRETAVG + 1.42*TLMTA - 20.26*NIMTAAVG. PRICE is log(min(abs(prc), 15)); MB is shrout*abs(prc)/ceqq; CASHMTA is cheq/(shrout*abs(prc) + ltq); RSIZE is log(shrout*abs(prc)/ sum of shrout*abs(prc) for the largest 500 companies each month); IdioRisk is defined above, EXRETAVG is the weighted average excess return (log(1 + ret) - log(1 + mktrf)) over the previous 12 months, with weight on month t-j being $\phi^j$ and the sum scaled by $\frac{1-\phi}{1-\phi^{12}}$; TLMTA is total liabilities (ltq/(shrout*abs(prc)); NIMTAAVG is a weighted average of net income over total assets (ibq/(shrout*abs(prc) + ltq)) over four quarters, with weight $\phi^q$ on quarter $t-q$ and the sum scaled by $\frac{1-\phi^3}{1-\phi^{12}}$. $\phi = 2^{-\frac{1}{3}}$. All input variables are winsorized at the 5th and 95th percentile. Exclude if price less than 1.

records.name: Long-term EPS forecast (Monthly)
records.signal_description: Long-term EPS forecast (Monthly); Long-term earnings forecast (fgr5yr).  Exclude if book equity (ceq), net income (ib), deferred taxes (txdi), dividends (dvp), revenue (sale) or depreciation (dp) is missing.

records.name: Pension Funding Status
records.signal_description: Pension Funding Status; FR = (FVPA - PBO), scaled by total assets (at). FVPA is pbnaa from 1980 to 1986, pplao + pplao from 1987 to 1997, and pplao after 1997. PBO is pbnvv from 1980 to 1986, pbpro + pbpru from 1987 to 1997, and pbpro after 1997. Exclude if price less than 5 or  shrcd > 11.

records.name: gross profits / total assets
records.signal_description: gross profits / total assets; Revenue (sale) - cost of goods solds (cogs), divided by 12 months lagged total assets.

records.name: gross profits / total assets
records.signal_description: gross profits / total assets; Revenue (revtq) - cost of goods solds (cogsq), divided by one quarter lagged total assets (atq).

records.name: Investment growth (1 year)
records.signal_description: Investment growth (1 year); Growth between one-year lagged capital expenditures (capx) and two-year lagged capital expenditures. Replace capx with the one year difference in property, plant and equipment (ppent) if capx is missing and the corresponding firm age is greater or equal than two years.

records.name: Gross margin growth to sales growth
records.signal_description: Gross margin growth to sales growth; Define gross margin GM as revenue (sale) minus cost of goods sold (cogs). GrGMToGrSales is the percentage growth of GM relative to average GM in years t-1 and t-2, minus the percentage growth of revenue relative to average revenue in years t-1 and t-2. Replace growth rates with growth relative to the previous year only if data for t-2 are not available.

records.name: Change in sales vs change in receiv
records.signal_description: Change in sales vs change in receiv; Percentage growth in sales (sale) relative to average sales of t-1 and t-2, minus percentage growth in receivables (rect) relative to average receivables of t-1 and t-2. Both growth terms are calculated relative to t-1 only if t-2 is missing.

records.name: Idiosyncratic risk (CAPM)
records.signal_description: Idiosyncratic risk (CAPM); Standard deviation of residuals from CAPM regressions using the past month of daily data.  Value weighted

records.name: Idiosyncratic risk (q factor)
records.signal_description: Idiosyncratic risk (q factor); Standard deviation of residuals from q-factor regressions using the past month of daily data.  Value weighted

records.name: Intrinsic or historical value
records.signal_description: Intrinsic or historical value; Value based on a two-stage dividend discount model assuming ROE is remains the same as the most recent observation, scaled by market value.

records.name: Kaplan Zingales index quarterly
records.signal_description: Kaplan Zingales index quarterly; -1.002* (net income (ni) + depreciation (dp))/total assets (at) + .283*(total assets (at) + market value of equity - book value of equity (ceq) - deferred taxes (txdi))/total assets (at) + 3.319*(debt in current liabilities (dlc) + long-term debt (dltt))/(debt in current liabilities + long-term debt + book value of equity) - 39.368*(Dividends (divamt)/total assets) - 1.315*(cash and short-term investments (che)/total assets). Replace txdi and divamt with 0 if missing.

records.name: Laborforce efficiency
records.signal_description: Laborforce efficiency; One year growth of the ratio between sales (sale) and employment (emp).

records.name: Market leverage quarterly
records.signal_description: Market leverage quarterly; Total liabilities (lt) divided by market value of equity.

records.name: Number of analysts
records.signal_description: Number of analysts; Number of estimates (numest) in IBES for one-quarter ahead earnings. Replace with 0 if missing after 1989.

records.name: Net debt to price
records.signal_description: Net debt to price; Long-term debt (dltt) plus debt in current liabilities (dlc) plus preferred stock (pstk) plus preferred dividends in arrears (dvpa) minus treasury stock (tstkp) minus cash and short-term investments (che), scaled by market value of equity. Exclude if SIC between 6000 and 6999, or if missing value for total assets (at), net income (ib), common shares outstanding (csho), book value of equity (ceq) or price close fiscal year (prcc\_f).  Keep only 3rd B/M Quintile, following Table 4 (and in contrast to Table 1).

records.name: Net Payout Yield quarterly
records.signal_description: Net Payout Yield quarterly; Dividends (dvc) plus purchase of common and preferred stock (prstkc) minus sale of common and preferred stock (sstk), divided by market value of equity.

records.name: operating profits / book equity
records.signal_description: operating profits / book equity; Revenue (revt) minus cost (cogs) - administrative expenses (xsga) - interest expenses (xint), scaled by lagged book value of equity (ceq). Exclude smallest size tercile.

records.name: operating profits / book equity
records.signal_description: operating profits / book equity; Revenue (revtq) minus cost (cogsq) - administrative expenses (xsgaq) - interest expenses (xintq), scaled by equity. Equity is shareholder equity (seqq) if not missing. Otherwise, the sum of book equity (ceqq) and preferred stock (pstkq) if not missing. Otherwise, assets (atq) minus liabilities (ltq).

records.name: Oper prof R&D adj lagged assets
records.signal_description: Oper prof R&D adj lagged assets; Revenue (revt) minus cost (cogs) - (administrative expenses (xsga) - R&D expenses (xrd)), all divided by total assets (at) in year t-1. Replace all variables in the numerator with 0 if they are missing. Exclude if share code is greater 11, market value of equity, BM or total assets are missing, or if SIC code between 6000 and 6999.

records.name: Oper prof R&D adj lagged assets (qtrly)
records.signal_description: Oper prof R&D adj lagged assets (qtrly); Revenue (revtq) minus cost (cogsq) - (administrative expenses (xsgaq) - R&D expenses (xrdq)), all divided by total assets (atq) in quarter t-1. Replace all variables in the numerator with 0 if they are missing. Exclude if share code is greater 11, market value of equity, BM or total assets are missing, or if SIC code between 6000 and 6999.

records.name: Operating leverage (qtrly)
records.signal_description: Operating leverage (qtrly); Sum of administrative expenses (xsga) and cost of goods sold (cogs), scaled by total assets (at).  Use xsga = 0 if xsga is missing.

records.name: Org cap w/o industry adjustment
records.signal_description: Org cap w/o industry adjustment; OrgCapAdj without the industry adjustment (see OrgCapAdj).

records.name: O Score quarterly
records.signal_description: O Score quarterly; OScore = -1.32 - .407*log(at/GNP deflator) + 6.03*(lt/at) - 1.43*( (act - lct)/at) + .076*(lct/act) - 1.72*I(lt > at) - 2.37*(ib/at) - 1.83*(fopt/lt) + .285*(ib + ib$_{t-12}$ + ib$_{t-24}$ < 0) -  .521*( (ib - ib$_{t-12}$)/(abs(ib) + .abs(ib$_{t-12}$)) ). fopt = oancf if fopt is missing.  Exclude Exclude if SIC code between 3999 and 4999, or greater than 5999. Exclude if price less than 5.  Then exclude if OScore is in bottom quintile of OScore (original paper shows non-monotonic returns, as does our replication)

records.name: Payout Yield quarterly
records.signal_description: Payout Yield quarterly; Sum of dividends (dvc), purchase of common and preferred stock (prstkc) and max(preferred stock redemption value (pstkrv), 0), divided by lag(market value of equity, 6 months).  Exclude if PayoutYield $\leq$ 0.

records.name: Change in Current Ratio
records.signal_description: Change in Current Ratio; One year growth of the current ratio (currat) defined as current total assets (act) divided by current total liabilities (lct).

records.name: Change in depreciation to PPE
records.signal_description: Change in depreciation to PPE; Annual percentage change in the ratio of depreciation (dp) to property, plant and equipment (ppent).

records.name: Change in gross margin vs sales
records.signal_description: Change in gross margin vs sales; growth in (sale-cogs) minus growth in sale

records.name: Change in quick ratio
records.signal_description: Change in quick ratio; One year growth in quick ratio, defined as change between total current assets (act) and inventory (invt) scaled by the total current liabilities (lct).

records.name: Change in sales to inventory
records.signal_description: Change in sales to inventory; One year growth in sales (sale) to inventory (invt) ratio.

records.name: Profit Margin
records.signal_description: Profit Margin; Net income (ni) over revenue (revt). Exclude if price less than 5.

records.name: Profit Margin
records.signal_description: Profit Margin; Net income (ni) over revenue (revt). Exclude if price less than 5.

records.name: Piotroski F-score
records.signal_description: Piotroski F-score; Sum of nine indicator variables which are: 1 if net income (ib) greater 0; 1 if net cash flow (oancf) greater 0; 1 if return on assets (ib/at) increased relative to previous year; 1 if net cash flow greater net income; 1 if long-term debt to assets (dltt/at) declined over the previous year;  if current assets to current liabilities (act/lct) increased over the previous year; 1 if ebit/sale (ebit = ib + txt + xint) increased over the previous year; 1 if revenue to assets increased over the previous year; 1 if shrout $\leq$ shrout last year. Include highest quintile of book-to-market only.  Exclude if missing any of the input variables.

records.name: Quick ratio
records.signal_description: Quick ratio; Difference between current total assets (act) and total inventory (invt) all divided by the current total liabilities (lct).

records.name: R&D over market cap quarterly
records.signal_description: R&D over market cap quarterly; R&D expense (xrd) over market value of equity.

records.name: R&D to sales
records.signal_description: R&D to sales; One year lagged quarterly R&D (xrdq) divided by one year lagged quarterly sales (saleq).

records.name: 6 month residual momentum
records.signal_description: 6 month residual momentum; Run a rolling regression over 36 months of excess return (retrf) on excess market return (mktrf), size and value factors (smb, hml) and compute idiosyncratic returns as the one-month lagged residual. ResidualMomentum is the rolling mean of the residual divided by the rolling standard deviation of the residual, both computed over the past 6 months.

records.name: Return on Net Operating Assets
records.signal_description: Return on Net Operating Assets; Net income (ni) over revenue (revt). Exclude if price less than 5.

records.name: Return on Net Operating Assets
records.signal_description: Return on Net Operating Assets; Net income (ni) over revenue (revt). Exclude if price less than 5.

records.name: Idiosyncratic skewness (CAPM)
records.signal_description: Idiosyncratic skewness (CAPM); Skewness of idiosyncratic returns computed as residuals from regression of daily excess returns (ret - rf) on market factor (mktrf) over the previous month. We require at least 15 non-missing observations.

records.name: Idiosyncratic skewness (Q model)
records.signal_description: Idiosyncratic skewness (Q model); Skewness of idiosyncratic returns computed as residuals from regression of daily excess returns (ret - rf) on q-factors (r\_mkt, r\_me, r\_ia, r\_roe) over the previous month. We require at least 15 non-missing observations. We download q-factor data from \url{http://global-q.org/index.html}.

records.name: RoA volatility
records.signal_description: RoA volatility; Rolling standard deviation of quarterly return on assets (roaq) over 4 years (minimum 2 years).

records.name: Sales to cash ratio
records.signal_description: Sales to cash ratio; Sales (sale) divided by cash and short-term investments (che).

records.name: Sales to inventory
records.signal_description: Sales to inventory; Sales (sale) divded by total inventory (invt).

records.name: Sales to receivables
records.signal_description: Sales to receivables; Sales (sale) divded by total receivables (rect).

records.name: Secured debt
records.signal_description: Secured debt; Debt/mortgages and other secured (dm) divided by long-term liabilities (dltt) plus current liabilities (dlc). Replace with 0 if missing.

records.name: Secured debt indicator
records.signal_description: Secured debt indicator; Binary version of secured. 1 if secured greater than 0, 0 otherwise.

records.name: Annual sales growth
records.signal_description: Annual sales growth; Sales (sale) relative to t-1.

records.name: Annual sales growth quarterly
records.signal_description: Annual sales growth quarterly; Sales (sale) relative to t-1.

records.name: Sales-to-price quarterly
records.signal_description: Sales-to-price quarterly; Ratio of annual sales (sale) to market value of equity.

records.name: Tangibility quarterly
records.signal_description: Tangibility quarterly; Cash and short-term investments (che) plus .715*receivables (rect) + .547*inventory (invt) + .535* property, plant and equipment (ppent), scaled by total assets (at). Only defined for manufacturing firms (SIC $\geq$ 2000 and SIC <4000). Exclude the lowest tercile of manufacturing firms by total assets.

records.name: Taxable income to income (qtrly)
records.signal_description: Taxable income to income (qtrly); Ratio of Taxes paid and tax share of net income. Numerator is defined as the sum of foreign (txfo) and federal (txfed) income taxes. If either one is missing, numerator is defined as total taxes (txt) minus deferred taxes (txdi). Denominator is the product of the prevailing tax rate and net income (ib). Tax rate is .48 before 1979, .46 from 1979 to 1986, .4 in 1987, .34 between 1988 and 1992 and .35 from 1993 onwards. If net income is negative, and the numerator is positive, tax is defined as 1. Exclude if price less than 5.

records.name: Whited-Wu index
records.signal_description: Whited-Wu index; Group data by 3 digit SIC code and month to compute total sales (saleq) by industry. Calculate the Whited-Wu index as -0.091*(quarterly income before extraordninary items (ibq) + quarterly depreciation and amortizarion (dpq)) / (quarterly assets(atq)) - 0.062( if the quarterly dividends per share (dvpsxq) is not missing and greater than 0) + 0.021 * quarterly long-term debt (dlttq) / atq - 0.044 * log(atq) + 0.102 * (four-quarter growth of quarterly Industry Sales) - 0.035 * (one-quarter growth of quarterly sales (saleq)).

records.name: Altman Z-Score quarterly
records.signal_description: Altman Z-Score quarterly; 1.2*(current assets (act) - current liabilities (lct))/total assets (at) + 1.4*(Retained earnings (re)/total assets (at)) + 3.3*(net income (ni) + interest expense (xint) + total taxes (txt))/total assets (at) +  .6*(market value of equity/Total liabilities (lt)) + revenue (revt)/ total assets (at). Include only NYSE stocks. Exclude if SIC code between 4000 and 4999, or above 5999.  Exclude if ZScore is in bottom quintile of ZScore (original paper shows non-monotonic returns, as does our replication)

records.name: Time-series momentum (TSMOM)
records.signal_description: An instrument's own past 12-month excess return predicts its future return across 58 liquid futures/forward contracts spanning equity indices, currencies, commodities, and government bonds; persistence for 1-12 months partially reverses over longer horizons; a diversified TSMOM portfolio delivers substantial abnormal returns with little exposure to standard factors (Quantpedia third-party replication: Sharpe 1.31). Distinct from cross-sectional momentum (CZ Mom12m): conditions on own past return sign, not cross-sectional rank.
records.source: Moskowitz, Ooi and Pedersen, Journal of Financial Economics 104, 228-250

records.name: Weekly short-term reversal (contrarian)
records.signal_description: Stocks that were winners (losers) over the prior week experience sizeable return reversals the next week: NYSE/AMEX July 1962-Dec 1986 winner portfolios averaged -0.35 to -0.55%/week the following week, loser portfolios +0.86 to +1.24%/week; contrarian abnormal returns over 2%/month survive bid-ask and plausible cost corrections. Weekly-frequency variant of the monthly reversal covered by cz_STreversal (Jegadeesh 1990, extreme-decile spread 2.49%/month 1934-1987).

records.name: Betting against beta (BAB)
records.signal_description: Self-financing factor long leveraged low-beta and short de-leveraged high-beta US stocks realized a Sharpe ratio of 0.78 over 1926-March 2012 (~2x value, 40% above momentum); the analogous US Treasury maturity-sorted BAB realized Sharpe 0.81; also documented in 19 other MSCI markets, corporate bonds, and futures. Cross-sectional US-equity beta variants covered by cz_Beta and cz_BetaFP; this record is the multi-asset leveraged-factor construction.
records.source: Frazzini and Pedersen, Journal of Financial Economics 111, 1-25

records.name: Carry (diversified multi-asset factor)
records.signal_description: A security's model-free 'carry' (futures/spot or yield-based expected return if prices stay constant) predicts returns cross-sectionally and in time series across asset classes; individual asset-class carry strategies average an annualized Sharpe of 0.8 and a diversified portfolio of carry strategies across all asset classes earns a Sharpe of 1.2 (published JFE version); not explained by known predictors.
records.source: Koijen, Moskowitz, Pedersen and Vrugt, Journal of Financial Economics 127(2), 197-225

records.name: FX carry (currency interest-rate differential)
records.signal_description: Currency carry -- buying high-interest-rate and selling low-interest-rate currencies -- as one of the asset-class carry strategies documented by Koijen-Moskowitz-Pedersen-Vrugt; asset-class carry strategies average an annualized Sharpe of 0.8.
records.source: Koijen, Moskowitz, Pedersen and Vrugt, Journal of Financial Economics 127(2), 197-225

records.name: Commodity carry (basis / backwardation-contango)
records.signal_description: Commodity futures carry from the futures-curve basis (backwardation vs contango) predicts commodity returns cross-sectionally and in time series; part of the KMPV global carry evidence across commodities.
records.source: Koijen, Moskowitz, Pedersen and Vrugt, Journal of Financial Economics 127(2), 197-225

records.name: Bond carry (yield/roll-down, global bonds and US Treasuries)
records.signal_description: Carry in global government bonds and US Treasuries (yield plus roll-down) predicts bond returns cross-sectionally and in time series; part of the KMPV global carry evidence.
records.source: Koijen, Moskowitz, Pedersen and Vrugt, Journal of Financial Economics 127(2), 197-225

records.name: Equity index carry (implied dividend/futures basis)
records.signal_description: Carry in global equity indices, defined from equity futures prices / expected dividend yields, predicts index returns cross-sectionally and in time series; part of the KMPV global carry evidence.
records.source: Koijen, Moskowitz, Pedersen and Vrugt, Journal of Financial Economics 127(2), 197-225

records.name: Credit carry
records.signal_description: Carry in credit markets predicts returns cross-sectionally and in time series; part of the KMPV global carry evidence spanning global equities, bonds, commodities, US Treasuries, credit, and options.
records.source: Koijen, Moskowitz, Pedersen and Vrugt, Journal of Financial Economics 127(2), 197-225

records.name: Options carry
records.signal_description: Carry in index/equity options predicts returns; part of the KMPV global carry evidence spanning global equities, bonds, commodities, US Treasuries, credit, and options.
records.source: Koijen, Moskowitz, Pedersen and Vrugt, Journal of Financial Economics 127(2), 197-225

records.name: Turn-of-the-month effect
records.signal_description: Essentially all of the US equity excess return over 1897-2005 accrued in the four-day window from the last trading day of the month through the next three days; during the other 16 trading days investors received no reward for bearing market risk; not confined to small/low-priced stocks, quarter-ends, or the US.
records.source: Lakonishok and Smidt, Review of Financial Studies 1(4), 403-425; Xu and McConnell, 2008

records.name: January effect (small-firm January seasonal)
records.signal_description: Equal-weighted NYSE returns averaged ~3.5% in January vs ~0.5% in other months (1904-1974); nearly 50% of the small-firm size premium over 1963-1979 came from January abnormal returns.
records.source: Rozeff and Kinney, Journal of Financial Economics 3, 379-402; Keim, Journal of Financial Economics 12, 13-32

records.name: Halloween effect / Sell-in-May
records.signal_description: November-April returns significantly exceed May-October returns in 36 of 37 country stock markets studied over 1970-1998, across Europe, North America, Asia, Africa, Australia.
records.source: Bouman and Jacobsen, American Economic Review 92(5), 1618-1635

records.name: Day-of-week / weekend (Monday) effect
records.signal_description: Mean Monday returns on the S&P were negative over 1953-1977 and in every five-year subperiod, while the other four weekdays averaged positive returns; rejects both calendar-time and trading-time models.

records.name: Pre-holiday effect
records.signal_description: The trading day before holidays showed mean returns nine to fourteen times the average of remaining days (NYSE/AMEX 1963-1982); out of sample (1983-2019) the premium survives only among small firms (Ko and Yang, Critical Finance Review 13(3-4), 531-538, 2024).

records.name: Same-calendar-month seasonal momentum (Heston-Sadka)
records.signal_description: Stocks with relatively high (low) returns in a given calendar month tend to repeat that performance in the same month in future years, up to 20 annual lags; seasonal strategies average over 50 bp/month; independent of size, industry, earnings announcements, dividends, fiscal year. Cross-sectional monthly implementations covered in CZ as cz_MomSeason / MomSeasonShort / MomSeason06YrPlus etc.; this record anchors the general effect for non-CZ variants.
records.source: Heston and Sadka, Journal of Financial Economics 87, 418-445

records.name: Return seasonalities beyond US single stocks
records.signal_description: A strategy selecting stocks on historical same-calendar-month returns earns ~13%/year; seasonalities also appear in anomaly portfolios, commodities, international stock indices, and at daily frequency, and overwhelm unconditional differences in expected returns -- almost any periodic conditioning of returns has a documented near-neighbor here.
records.source: Keloharju, Linnainmaa and Nyberg, NBER Working Paper 20815

records.name: Overnight vs intraday equity premium decomposition
records.signal_description: Over 1993-2006 the entire US equity premium was earned close-to-open (overnight); open-to-close (intraday) returns were near zero or negative; holds for individual stocks, indexes, and index futures on NYSE and Nasdaq; partly driven by high opening prices declining in the first trading hour.
records.source: Cooper, Cliff and Gulen, SSRN working paper 1004081

records.name: Overnight/intraday 'tug of war' strategy decomposition
records.signal_description: Overnight and intraday return components each persist for years but offset each other; across 14 strategies profits accrue either entirely overnight (momentum and short-term reversal) or entirely intraday (value-type and most other anomalies), typically with opposite signs in the other session; e.g. short-term reversal overnight alpha +0.93%/month (t=4.28) vs intraday CAPM alpha -1.05% (t=-3.25).
records.source: Lou, Polk and Skouras, Journal of Financial Economics 134(1), 192-213

records.name: Overnight drift in equity index futures (hour-resolved)
records.signal_description: More than half of S&P 500 futures returns accrue in the 16:15-9:30 overnight session (~3.6% p.a.), with ~3.7% p.a. earned in the 2:00-3:00 a.m. hour alone around European open; linked to inventory risk and close-of-day order imbalances, with strong positive overnight reversals after selloffs. The 2:00-3:00 window has averaged close to zero since 2021 (NY Fed Liberty Street, July 2026).
records.source: Boyarchenko, Larsen and Whelan, Federal Reserve Bank of New York Staff Report 917

records.name: Opening gap / close-to-open gap effects
records.signal_description: Close-to-open gap behavior is documented prior art via the overnight-return literature: the equity premium accrues in the overnight gap (Cooper-Cliff-Gulen 2008), high opening prices systematically decline in the first trading hour, and overnight sessions show strong positive reversals after selloffs (Boyarchenko-Larsen-Whelan SR 917). Any daily-bar gap-fade or gap-continuation signal built from close-to-open vs open-to-close returns is presumptively covered by this family.
records.source: Cooper, Cliff and Gulen, SSRN 1004081; Boyarchenko, Larsen and Whelan, NY Fed Staff Report 917

records.name: Customer-supplier momentum (economic-links lead-lag)
records.signal_description: Buying suppliers after positive news to their principal customers yields monthly long-short alphas over 150 bp, robust to three-factor model, liquidity, own-firm momentum, industry momentum, and within-industry lead-lag controls; mechanism is investor inattention to firm-level economic links. Cross-sectional monthly implementation covered in CZ as cz_CustomerMomentum; related IO-link variants cz_iomom_cust / cz_iomom_supp (Menzly-Ozbas 2010).
records.source: Cohen and Frazzini, Journal of Finance 63(4), 1977-2011

records.name: Industry momentum
records.signal_description: Buying stocks in past winning industries and selling past losing industries is highly profitable (US, July 1963-July 1995) and accounts for much of individual-stock momentum; survives size, book-to-market, individual momentum, dispersion, and microstructure controls. Cross-sectional implementation covered in CZ as cz_IndMom; anchors non-US/non-monthly variants.
records.source: Moskowitz and Grinblatt, Journal of Finance 54(4), 1249-1290

records.name: Size-based lead-lag (large stocks lead small)
records.signal_description: Returns of large stocks lead those of small stocks; weekly portfolio returns are strongly positively autocorrelated despite negative individual autocorrelations, so contrarian profits can arise from cross-autocovariances even without individual-stock overreaction.
records.source: Lo and MacKinlay, Review of Financial Studies 3(2), 175-205

records.name: Intra-industry size lead-lag (big leads small within industry)
records.signal_description: The big-firms-lead-small-firms effect is predominantly an intra-industry phenomenon driven by slow diffusion of (especially negative) industry information; strongest in small, less competitive, neglected industries; related to small firms' drift after big firms' earnings releases (cf. CZ cz_IndRetBig, cz_EarnSupBig from Hou 2007).

records.name: Pairs trading (distance method)
records.signal_description: Matching stocks into pairs by normalized historical price distance and trading divergences yields average annualized excess returns up to 11% on self-financing portfolios; profits typically exceed conservative transaction-cost estimates and are distinct from previously documented reversal profits.
records.source: Gatev, Goetzmann and Rouwenhorst, Review of Financial Studies 19(3), 797-827

records.name: High-volume return premium (volume-attention)
records.signal_description: Stocks with unusually high (low) trading volume over a day or week tend to appreciate (depreciate) over the following month, consistent with a visibility/attention mechanism; not explained by return autocorrelations, announcements, market risk, or liquidity. Not in the CZ predictor list.
records.source: Gervais, Kaniel and Mingelgrin, Journal of Finance 56, 877-919

records.name: 52-week high momentum
records.signal_description: Nearness of the current price to the 52-week high explains a large share of momentum profits, dominates past-return measures (individual and industry), and unlike conventional momentum does not reverse long-run. Cross-sectional implementation covered in CZ as cz_High52; anchors variants in other assets or frequencies.
records.source: George and Hwang, Journal of Finance 59, 2145-2176

records.name: Amihud illiquidity (ILLIQ) pricing
records.signal_description: ILLIQ -- average daily |return| / dollar volume -- prices stocks cross-sectionally (illiquid stocks earn higher returns; survives beta, size, volatility, dividend-yield, and past-return controls) and in time series (expected market illiquidity raises ex-ante excess returns). Cross-sectional implementation covered in CZ as cz_Illiquidity; this record anchors the time-series/market-level channel.

records.name: Variance risk premium (short index variance)
records.signal_description: Synthetic variance swap rates on stock indexes systematically exceed subsequently realized variance, so selling index variance earns a premium; index variance risk premia are negative with excess returns unexplained by CAPM or Fama-French factors (significant negative alphas); studied on five stock indexes and 35 individual stocks.
records.source: Carr and Wu, Review of Financial Studies 22, 1311-1341

records.name: VIX futures basis harvesting (short contango)
records.signal_description: The VIX futures basis does not forecast spot VIX changes but does forecast VIX futures price changes; shorting VIX futures in contango and buying in backwardation, hedged with mini-S&P futures, was highly profitable over Jan 2006-Dec 2011 and robust to transaction costs.
records.source: Simon and Campasano, Journal of Derivatives 21(3), 54-69

records.name: Index reconstitution / addition-deletion premium
records.signal_description: Over 1990-2005, S&P 500 and Russell 2000 additions rose on average +8.8% and +4.7% from announcement to effective day (deletions -15.1% and -4.6%), imposing index-turnover costs of 21-28 bp/yr (S&P 500) and 38-77 bp/yr (Russell 2000) on index funds; premia peaked around 2000.

records.name: Index effect decay (post-2010 disappearance)
records.signal_description: The abnormal return on S&P 500 additions fell from an average of 7.4% in the 1990s to 0.3% in the most recent decade, and deletion effects shrank to a 0.1% magnitude, despite growth in indexed assets -- documented regime death of the reconstitution premium; 'known effect, now weaker/gone' is T1, not novel.
records.source: Greenwood and Sammon, Journal of Finance 80(2), 657-698

records.name: ETF premium/discount mean reversion
records.signal_description: ETF prices deviate from NAV within a band of ~200 bp (~100 bp after controlling for stale underlying prices via a cross-section of similar ETFs), larger for international/illiquid holdings; active strategies trading these deviations produced substantial pre-cost abnormal returns (short-term mean reversion in ETF prices).

records.name: LLM news-headline sentiment long-short
records.signal_description: GPT-4 scoring of news headlines predicts next-day stock returns out-of-sample (Oct 2021-May 2024): long positive-score / short negative-score earns an annualized Sharpe of 2.97 (pre-cost, equal-weighted; 1.29 at 10 bps round-trip, 0.56 value-weighted), vs 1.66 for GPT-3.5 and negative for small models; edge decays rapidly with LLM adoption -- Sharpe 6.54 (2021Q4) to 3.68 (2022), 2.33 (2023), 1.22 (Jan-May 2024). Decisive prior art for 'LLM reads news, trade the score'.

records.name: 101 Formulaic Alphas (WorldQuant)
records.signal_description: Published explicit formulas-as-code for 101 real-life quantitative trading alphas proprietary to WorldQuant; short algebraic expressions over open/high/low/close/volume/vwap/returns/adv{d} using rank, Ts_Rank, correlation, delta, sign, log, decay_linear, IndNeutralize; average holding periods 0.6-6.4 days, average pairwise correlation 15.9%. Defines the canonical signal-form vocabulary for daily cross-sectional price-volume alphas; candidates expressible in this grammar are presumptively crowded.

records.name: Genetic-programming technical rules in FX (Neely-Weller-Dittmar)
records.signal_description: GP-evolved technical trading rules for six dollar exchange rates over 1981-1995 found economically significant out-of-sample excess returns of roughly 1-7% per year -- the canonical positive result for evolutionary rule search, in FX rather than equities.
records.source: Neely, Weller and Dittmar, Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis 32, 405-426

records.name: Genetic algorithms for technical trading rules (Allen-Karjalainen)
records.signal_description: GP-evolved ex-ante technical trading rules for the S&P 500 showed some predictive ability but no evidence of excess returns over buy-and-hold after transaction costs (0.25% one-way) -- the canonical negative equity-market result for evolutionary rule search.
records.source: Allen and Karjalainen, Journal of Financial Economics 51(2), 245-271

records.name: Data-snooping-adjusted rule-universe testing (White's Reality Check)
records.signal_description: Applied White's Reality Check bootstrap to 7,846 technical trading rules on 100 years of daily DJIA data: the best in-sample rule survives an in-sample snooping adjustment but its superior performance is not repeated out-of-sample 1987-1996, and no rule outperforms on S&P 500 futures (1984-1996). Ancestor of all family-wise-adjusted signal-search evaluation.
records.source: Sullivan, Timmermann and White, Journal of Finance 54(5), 1647-1691

records.name: Calendar-effect rule mining under data-snooping adjustment
records.signal_description: Evaluated 9,452 calendar-based trading rules and found that calendar effects (Monday effect, January effect, etc.) that appear highly significant in isolation are no longer significant once evaluated against the full universe of rules that could have been considered.
records.source: Sullivan, Timmermann and White, Journal of Econometrics 105(1), 249-286

records.name: Execution-slippage re-examination of technical-rule profits
records.signal_description: Re-examined Allen-Karjalainen GP rules and Brock-Lakonishok-LeBaron moving-average rules: reported profits were likely unachievable due to price slippage between signal measurement and execution and understated transaction costs; the apparent after-cost success of the BLL rules is a spurious result of data snooping.

records.name: Brute-force accounting-ratio mining (29,000 ratios)
records.signal_description: Naive data mining of 29,000 accounting ratios keeping t > 2.0 produces out-of-sample cross-sectional return predictability similar to the peer-reviewed literature; for both, ~50% of predictability remains after the original sample periods -- peer review adds little beyond brute-force mining, and ~50% decay is the generic fate of any significant in-sample signal.

records.name: gplearn-style GP alpha mining with time-series operators
records.signal_description: Symbolic regression evolving expression trees by mutation/crossover, extended with formulaic-alpha time-series operators; attributed as the first genetic-programming method for alpha factors and the standard practitioner/academic baseline for formulaic alpha mining, still being refined (e.g. warm-start GP with structural constraints, arXiv 2412.00896).
records.source: Lin, Chen, Li and He, Huatai Securities Research Center technical report (per AlphaForge arXiv 2406.18394 and AlphaGen arXiv 2306.12964)

records.name: AutoAlpha: hierarchical evolutionary alpha mining with PCA-QD
records.signal_description: Pre-LLM hierarchical evolutionary algorithm for mining formulaic alphas: warm-start initialization from 'root genes', PCA-based Quality-Diversity search pushing exploration away from already-mined regions, and replacement to avoid premature convergence; evaluated on Chinese stock data.
records.source: Zhang, Li, Jin and Li, arXiv 2002.08245

records.name: AlphaEvolve (SIGMOD 2021): AutoML evolutionary alpha search
records.signal_description: AutoML-style evolutionary search over scalar/vector/matrix operators evolving a new class of alphas between formulaic and machine-learning alphas, with high returns and weak correlations (best evolved alpha Sharpe 21.32 vs 4.11 for a domain-expert alpha in the experiment tables). Unrelated to DeepMind's later system of the same name.
records.source: Cui, Wang, Zhang et al., SIGMOD 2021; arXiv 2103.16196

records.name: AlphaGen: RL over expression grammar with set-level reward
records.signal_description: Mines formulaic alphas with reinforcement learning where the downstream combination model's performance is the reward -- optimizing a synergistic SET of alphas rather than individual expressions; beats gplearn GP, single-alpha PPO, XGBoost, LightGBM and MLP on CSI300/CSI500; emits short algebraic expressions over daily OHLCV+vwap with cross-section and time-series operators (Ref, Mean, Std, Corr, Delta, WMA, EMA, ...).
records.source: Yu, Xue, Ao et al., KDD 2023 ADS track; arXiv 2306.12964

records.name: RiskMiner: risk-seeking MCTS alpha mining
records.signal_description: Formulates formulaic alpha discovery as a reward-dense MDP solved by risk-seeking Monte Carlo Tree Search, accounting for correlations within the mined alpha collection; pure-search (non-LLM) variant.

records.name: AlphaForge: generative-predictive network mining with dynamic reweighting
records.signal_description: Two-stage formulaic alpha framework: a generative-predictive neural network searches formula space, then the combination model incorporates temporal factor performance and dynamically adjusts weights rather than using fixed combination weights.

records.name: Alpha-GPT: LLM interactive alpha-mining copilot
records.signal_description: Established the 'LLM as interactive alpha-mining copilot' paradigm: prompt-engineered LLMs translate quant researchers' natural-language ideas into formulaic alphas, positioned against both hand-crafting and genetic-programming factor search.
records.source: Wang, Yuan, Zhou, Ni, Shum and Guo, arXiv 2308.00016

records.name: Alpha-GPT 2.0: human-in-the-loop multi-agent quant pipeline
records.signal_description: Extends Alpha-GPT to a human-in-the-loop multi-agent system spanning the full quant pipeline -- alpha mining, alpha modeling (combination), and alpha analysis -- with specialized LLM agents at each stage.

records.name: QuantAgent: two-loop self-improving LLM signal miner
records.signal_description: LLM agent for mining trading signals via a two-layer self-improving loop -- inner loop refining outputs against a knowledge base, outer loop testing outputs in the real world to grow the knowledge base -- with a claim of provably efficient convergence toward optimal behavior.
records.source: Wang, Yuan, Ni and Guo, arXiv 2402.03755

records.name: AlphaAgent: decay-resistant factors with AST-based originality enforcement
records.signal_description: Targets alpha decay explicitly with three regularizers: originality enforcement via abstract-syntax-tree similarity against existing factors, hypothesis-factor semantic alignment judged by an LLM, and AST-based complexity control -- automated novelty checking of generated alphas is itself published prior art.

records.name: Chain-of-Alpha: dual-chain LLM factor generation/optimization
records.signal_description: Fully automated dual-chain LLM framework -- a Factor Generation Chain producing candidate formulaic alphas and a Factor Optimization Chain refining them with backtest feedback -- evaluated on Chinese A-share benchmarks; withdrawn by arXiv for licensing/submission-rights issues but documented prior art.

records.name: LLM-in-MCTS symbolic alpha search ('Navigating the Alpha Jungle')
records.signal_description: Embeds an LLM inside Monte Carlo Tree Search: iteratively generates and refines symbolic alpha formulas within MCTS-driven exploration guided by quantitative backtest feedback, with frequent-subtree avoidance to force diversity.

records.name: QuantEvolve: quality-diversity evolution of full trading strategies
records.signal_description: Quality-diversity evolutionary search with a hypothesis-driven multi-agent LLM system evolving entire trading strategies (not just factor formulas), maintaining a feature map over strategy type, risk, and return characteristics; released a dataset of evolved strategies.
records.source: Yun, Lee and Jeon, arXiv 2510.18569; ACM ICAIF 2025 workshop oral

records.name: FactorMiner: self-evolving agent with skill architecture and experience memory
records.signal_description: Couples a Modular Skill Architecture (systematic financial evaluation as executable tools) with a structured Experience Memory distilling past mining trials, explicitly targeting the 'Correlation Red Sea' redundancy problem while producing a diverse library of high-quality factors.

records.name: AlphaPROBE: DAG-structured factor evolution with Bayesian retrieval
records.signal_description: Models factor discovery as a directed acyclic graph of factors with evolutionary relationships as edges; a Bayesian Factor Retriever picks seed factors balancing exploitation/exploration and a DAG-aware generator produces non-redundant refinements; beats eight baselines on Chinese stock data.

records.name: FunSearch: LLM-proposer + evaluator evolutionary loop
records.signal_description: Existence proof that an LLM-proposer + automated-evaluator evolutionary loop can exceed known state of the art in domains with exact evaluators: new cap-set constructions (largest increase in cap-set size in 20 years) and better bin-packing heuristics; the open question is whether a noisy market evaluator permits the same.
records.source: Romera-Paredes et al. (Google DeepMind), Nature, December 2023

records.name: AlphaEvolve (DeepMind): Gemini-powered evolutionary coding agent
records.signal_description: LLM+evaluator evolutionary coding agent that found a 4x4 complex-matrix multiplication algorithm using 48 scalar multiplications and improved on best-known solutions in ~20% of 50+ open math problems; method-level prior art for LLM-driven search exceeding training corpora against exact evaluators.

records.name: BloombergGPT: domain financial LLM
records.signal_description: 50-billion-parameter LLM trained on a 363-billion-token Bloomberg financial corpus plus 345 billion general-purpose tokens, targeting financial NLP (sentiment analysis, NER, question answering); domain LLM infrastructure, not a published alpha-mining or trading-signal system.

records.name: FinGPT: open-source financial LLM framework
records.signal_description: Open-source, data-centric financial LLM framework positioned as the accessible alternative to BloombergGPT, with stated applications in robo-advising, algorithmic trading, and low-code financial development; presented at the FinLLM Symposium at IJCAI 2023.

records.name: Post-knowledge-cutoff evaluation protocol for LLM signals
records.signal_description: Evaluating LLM trading signals only on post-knowledge-cutoff data to avoid lookahead bias and memorization is documented prior art: Lopez-Lira and Tang apply it explicitly, citing Sarkar and Vafa (2024) and Lopez-Lira, Tang and Zhu (2025); post-cutoff provenance discipline is a documented method, not a novel contribution.
records.source: Sarkar and Vafa 2024; Lopez-Lira, Tang and Zhu 2025 (per Lopez-Lira and Tang, arXiv 2304.07619)
